# Filter out rows that are not actual seasons (like "Totals:" or "No Team")
df = df[~df['Season'].astype(str).str.contains('Totals|No Team|Upcoming', na=False)]

# Convert 'Season' to numeric, errors='coerce' will turn non-numeric to NaN
df['Season'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Season'], errors='coerce')

# Drop rows where 'Season' is NaN (just in case)
df = df.dropna(subset=['Season'])

# Convert 'Total Wins' to numeric, coerce errors to NaN
df['Total Wins'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Total Wins'], errors='coerce')

# Find the row(s) with the maximum total wins
max_wins = df['Total Wins'].max()
max_wins_rows = df[df['Total Wins'] == max_wins]

# Get the season(s) with the most total wins
seasons_with_max_wins = max_wins_rows['Season'].astype(int).tolist()

# If there are multiple seasons with the same max wins, return all
answer = seasons_with_max_wins
